description: The backend shares the child's live location with a secondary guardian. If the secondary guardian does not need continuous real-time location access, or if access is granted too broadly in time, scope, or precision, the flow discloses more personal data than necessary.
assumptions: Assumes the secondary guardian role may not always require unrestricted live location access and that purpose/need-to-know constraints may be missing or weak.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on general LINDDUN Pro disclosure/minimisation concepts; exact subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Secondary guardian may be unaware of precise conditions and extent of location sharing
description: The backend grants access and shares live location, but the recipient may not be clearly informed about retention, refresh frequency, onward-sharing restrictions, or when access starts and ends. This reduces transparency around processing of the child's location data.
assumptions: Assumes the system may not clearly communicate usage conditions and limits when granting access.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit transparency/awareness mapping; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label may differ.

title: Secondary guardian can further disclose or expose the child's location to unauthorized parties
description: Once the secondary guardian receives live location data, they may intentionally or accidentally reveal it to others, for example by screenshots, shared devices, or verbal disclosure. The flow therefore creates a risk of onward disclosure beyond the intended recipient.
assumptions: Assumes limited downstream technical controls over what the external recipient does with received location information.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node under disclosure to unauthorized parties/onward sharing; exact node id may differ by threat-tree version.

title: Live location enables identification and tracking of the child
description: Sharing real-time location can directly identify the child’s current whereabouts and habitual places, making the child identifiable and trackable in the physical world, especially when combined with account or family context.
assumptions: Assumes the live location is associated with a known child profile or is otherwise attributable by the recipient.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability from data content; exact subtree id may vary.

title: Repeated live location updates allow linkability of movement patterns
description: Continuous or repeated location disclosures allow the secondary guardian to link multiple observations into movement profiles, routines, school/home locations, and behavioral patterns over time.
assumptions: Assumes the flow provides repeated or continuous updates rather than a one-time coarse location.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linking multiple events/records over time; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Location sharing with the secondary guardian may exceed the child's or primary guardian's consent expectations
description: Granting secondary guardian access to live location may occur without valid, specific, or current consent from the appropriate data subject or legal authority, or may continue after consent should have been withdrawn or limited.
assumptions: Assumes consent or another legal basis is required for sharing a child’s live location and that authorization lifecycle controls may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for consent/legal basis non-compliance; exact node id may vary.

title: Insufficient evidence about who granted or used secondary guardian access
description: If the backend does not maintain adequate records of access grant decisions and disclosures, parties may later deny that location access was granted, received, or used. This weakens accountability for sensitive location sharing.
assumptions: Assumes audit logging or provenance around authorization and disclosure events may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit repudiation/accountability node; exact subtree id may differ.

title: Partner can link shared analytics to its existing identifiers or datasets
description: Even if the backend shares only aggregated usage and engagement analytics, the advertising/analytics partner may combine cohort breakdowns, timestamps, campaign metadata, app version, region, or other dimensions with data it already holds to link the shared data to particular users, devices, or small groups.
assumptions: Assumes the partner receives segmented or sufficiently granular aggregates and has other datasets or identifiers available for matching.

title: Supposedly aggregated analytics may still allow singling out or re-identification
description: If aggregates are too fine-grained, cover small populations, or are shared repeatedly over time, the partner may infer information about identifiable users or devices from the analytics feed.
assumptions: Assumes low-count cohorts, rich dimensions, or differencing across multiple reports/releases.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability from insufficient aggregation/anonymization; exact node naming may differ.

title: Shared analytics can reveal sensitive behavior or interests
description: Usage and engagement analytics may expose patterns about what users do in the app, when they are active, and which features or content categories they engage with. For some apps, these patterns can disclose interests, habits, or sensitive inferences to the partner.
assumptions: Assumes analytics dimensions include feature/content categories, timestamps, geography, campaign source, or other behavior-rich signals.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for information disclosure to an unauthorized or over-privileged recipient; exact subtree id may differ.

title: Users may be unaware that their app activity funds the service through partner analytics sharing
description: Users may not realize that backend-collected usage data is shared onward with an external advertising/analytics partner for monetization, especially if notices are vague or buried.
assumptions: Assumes the app's privacy notice or in-app messaging does not clearly explain this onward sharing and purpose.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency about collection and sharing; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Analytics sharing for monetization may be incompatible with the original purpose or consent
description: Data collected to operate and improve the app may be repurposed and shared with an advertising/analytics partner to fund the free tier without a valid legal basis, adequate consent/opt-out, or purpose limitation controls.
assumptions: Assumes some jurisdictions or platform rules require consent, opt-out, contractual restrictions, or stricter purpose limitation for this type of sharing.

title: Granular or repeated aggregate reports enable inference through differencing
description: Even when each report is aggregated, repeated disclosures with slightly different filters, time windows, or cohort definitions can let the partner derive hidden underlying values about small groups or individual users by subtraction or trend analysis.
assumptions: Assumes multiple related reports or API queries are available over time and counts are not protected by thresholding/noise.

title: Identity disclosure of the child through authenticated SOS/check-in submission
description: The manual check-in / SOS message is attributable to a specific child account or device, revealing the child's identity to the backend and potentially to anyone with access to backend records. Because the message is sent specifically for parental monitoring, the child is directly identifiable in the transmitted event.
assumptions: Assumes the backend associates the message with a child profile, account, device identifier, or session token.

title: Disclosure of precise location in the SOS/check-in message
description: The flow explicitly contains the child's current location. Exposure of this flow to the backend, logs, intermediaries, operators, or unauthorized parties would reveal highly sensitive real-time location data.
assumptions: Assumes current location is transmitted with meaningful precision and may be stored, logged, or observable in transit or at the receiver.

title: Linkability of repeated check-ins and SOS events
description: Multiple check-in or SOS messages from the same child can be linked via account identifiers, device identifiers, tokens, or consistent metadata. This enables the backend to build a history of events and correlate them with other records.
assumptions: Assumes recurring messages carry stable identifiers or are received in an authenticated session.

title: Disclosure through backend logging and internal access
description: Once received, the backend may log the child's SOS content, timestamps, and precise location in application logs, analytics pipelines, support tools, or databases. Excessive internal access or inadequate access controls can expose sensitive child safety events.
assumptions: Assumes normal backend operations include request logging, persistence, monitoring, or administrative access.

title: Linkability between child safety events and other backend data
description: The backend can correlate SOS/check-in data with other datasets such as account information, device telemetry, IP addresses, usage history, and family relationships. This expands the ability to link the event across contexts beyond what is necessary to notify the parent.
assumptions: Assumes the backend has access to other user, device, or family-account records.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for cross-context linkability at the receiving process.

title: Inference of sensitive circumstances from SOS/check-in patterns
description: The backend can infer sensitive facts about the child or family from the timing, frequency, and location of manual check-ins or SOS events, such as daily routines, school attendance, distress situations, or unusual movement patterns, even if the message content is minimal.
assumptions: Assumes events are retained and analyzed over time.

title: Unawareness of backend processing and downstream use of child location/SOS data
description: The child may be unaware of how the backend processes, stores, shares, retains, or repurposes the SOS/check-in message and location after receipt, including internal analytics, retention periods, and operational access.
assumptions: Assumes notice is limited, hard to understand, or not presented in a child-appropriate way.

title: Non-compliance risk for processing child location and emergency messages
description: Processing precise location and safety-related communications from a child may violate data protection obligations if consent/authorization, necessity, proportionality, retention limits, security safeguards, or children's transparency requirements are not adequately met.
assumptions: Assumes the service is subject to child/privacy regulation and that governance controls may be incomplete.
